title: Public Project Proof Ledger
principle: Every project claim should state what can be inspected, what it proves, what it does not prove, and what evidence would strengthen it.

items.claim: The Operations Room demonstrates a public-safe Operational Intelligence investigation path from signals to transaction timing, evidence graph, hypotheses, evaluation gates, decision packet, and operator approval.
items.evidence: Visitors can inspect the synthetic OI-ROOM-001 flow, contradiction and missing-evidence states, per-hop transaction timing, review-state ledger, decision packet, and downloadable walkthrough using only approved public-safe material.
items.limitation: This proves public artifact discipline and investigation-model clarity; it does not prove production incident outcomes, customer impact reduction, or private deployment performance.
items.nextProof: Run an external reviewer walkthrough against the Evidence Pack worksheet and record observed reasoning losses, missing evidence, and decision-quality feedback.
items.reviewQuestion: Can an experienced SRE follow the case and explain what is observation, inference, contradiction, missing evidence, confirmed fact, and approved action?

items.claim: Ask Ravikanth demonstrates a bounded public AI interface over approved professional and Operational Intelligence content rather than a generic chatbot wrapper.
items.evidence: The assistant has deterministic fallback behavior, public-safety refusal, related-route recommendations, citation expectations, prompt-injection coverage, answer metadata, and {fixtureCount} passing trust fixtures.
items.limitation: This proves local trust-contract coverage and public-safe answer discipline; it does not prove live model synthesis quality, vector retrieval quality, or reviewer-labeled helpfulness in production.
items.nextProof: Compare fallback, vector retrieval, and model synthesis across the live answer rubric using safe metadata and reviewer labels.
items.reviewQuestion: Does the assistant cite public sources, expose uncertainty, refuse confidential prompts, and route the visitor to the right proof surface?

items.claim: The Transaction Graph Explorer expresses the thesis that operational reasoning should follow customer or workflow journeys, not isolated service dashboards.
items.evidence: The public map, transaction-journey pattern, doctrine layers, and related writing connect transactions, topology, ownership, evidence, operational memory, and impact reasoning.
items.limitation: This proves conceptual and information-architecture clarity; it does not yet provide a runnable public graph dataset, benchmarked journey reconstruction, or independent implementation evidence.
items.nextProof: Add a public-safe sample graph fixture or reviewer walkthrough only if it tests a distinct failure mode such as stale ownership, broken correlation, or misleading local service health.
items.reviewQuestion: Can a reviewer see why transaction context changes the investigation decision compared with a service-only view?

items.claim: The AI Evaluation Workbench turns trust into release-gated behavior checks for operational AI: grounding, refusal, routing, replay, and regression.
items.evidence: The public eval report, retrieval checks, Ask fixtures, live answer rubric, evidence pack, and build gates test deterministic behavior without publishing confidential prompt text.
items.limitation: This proves deterministic coverage and release discipline; it does not yet prove live model quality, production drift detection, or multi-reviewer agreement.
items.nextProof: Add reviewer-labeled answer sessions and model-comparison results without publishing raw prompts or unsupported aggregate quality scores.
items.reviewQuestion: Would a principal engineer trust the release gate to catch unsafe, uncited, misrouted, or overconfident answer regressions?
